papers.title: SMAT: Staged Multi-Agent Training for Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ IROS 2026 (to appear, per authors); arXiv preprint
papers.code_status: SMAT-Exo holds only a README ('Code coming soon'), 2 commits on 2026-07-15; Fitz-Yuan/SMAT is a project page (figures, PDF, videos), no code; paper promised code 'upon acceptance' (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: SMAT: Staged Multi-Agent Training for Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
papers.core_idea: Two PPO actors (26-muscle MyoAssist human; bilateral hip exo, 18-D hip-kinematics+torque-history input) share one critic through four stages: human gait, added exo mass, exo-only with frozen human (6 Nm), co-adaptation (25 Nm). Reports 10.1% simulated hip-activation drop; 5-subject hardware positive power.
papers.what_to_take: The published simulated targets: 10.1% mean right-hip activation reduction (RF −13.5%, iliopsoas −10.5%, hamstrings −9.7%, GMax −6.6%), Stage 2 vs Stage 4 at 25 Nm; ablations (Stage-4-only → near-zero torque); offline GT-dataset check.
papers.left_untested: No same-human exo-ON/OFF evaluation, no seeds or learning curves, no comparison with the closed-form maximiser of its own exo reward (û≈clip(ω/2 rad/s, ±0.8)), and the Stage 2→4 human reward change confounds the 10.1%.
papers.feasibility_notes: Rebuildable from 2608.00715 supplement in MyoAssist; authors' CPU cost ~28 h/100M steps (~550M steps total), so GPU port is essential.

papers.title: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) for Hip Exoskeletons: Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation of a Simulation-Trained Co-Adaptive Controller
papers.venue: arXiv preprint (extended version of the IROS paper; IEEE journal under review, per authors)
papers.code_status: no code; SMAT-Exo placeholder README only (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) for Hip Exoskeletons: Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation of a Simulation-Trained Co-Adaptive Controller
papers.core_idea: Same SMAT policy (peak ~12 Nm, 50 Hz, IMU kinematics) tested on 8 adults with indirect calorimetry: net metabolic rate −19.7% vs passive device, −9.1% vs no-exo; passive 5.94 kg device costs +13.1%; positive-power ratio 0.98; speed and terrain generalisation.
papers.what_to_take: Supplement gives most training details: Algorithm S1, stage-wise reward weights (Table S2), per-joint imitation weights (S3), PPO hyperparameters (S4), Stage-4 reward α=0.3, β=0.15, λs=2, δ=0.8, ωs=2 rad/s.
papers.left_untested: Hip ROM rose 44°→62° (+41%), consistent with negative-damping assistance, yet no velocity-law or phase-profile control arm; Ctrl-B results withheld; single speed metabolic test, n=8, no EMG.
papers.feasibility_notes: Hardware results not reproducible here; take its simulation settings and the reported ~1.3 W metabolic saving per W exo positive power.

papers.title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
papers.code_status: no repository; paper says code 'will be made publicly available'; Fitz-Yuan/mjlab_myosuite (created 2026-07-23) is an unmodified fork of MyoHub/mjlab_myosuite, 0 commits ahead (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
papers.core_idea: Distils four MyoLeg-80 imitation experts (walk, turn, run, backward) into one latent-conditioned policy, fine-tunes on stitched transitions, initialises a shared-weight per-leg exo network from a hip-moment predictor, then co-adapts both with PPO and a shared critic.
papers.what_to_take: The GPU recipe (MuJoCo Warp + mjlab + rsl_rl, 8192/2048 envs, 300/100 Hz, 3.7e4 steps/s on one Blackwell GPU) and exo reward: 3.0·net-moment offload + power term 0.3τ̄ω̄−0.15τ̄² + hip-activation + smoothness.
papers.left_untested: No metabolic or EMG data, no seeds; its power term again peaks at τ̄=ω̄, yet no velocity-law baseline tests whether co-adaptation (flexion peak ~10% later, negative power −65–81%) beats it.
papers.feasibility_notes: Experts took 22–37 h each on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell; a 32 GB 5090 likely needs fewer envs; single-skill walking suffices for Phase 1.

papers.api_title: Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation
papers.core_idea: Three networks trained simultaneously in simulation (motion imitation, muscle coordination, exo control) on a 50-DOF, 208-muscle model with domain randomisation; exo reward = reduced muscle activation; ~8 h on RTX 3090; reported −24.3/−13.1/−15.4% metabolic rate (walk/run/stairs).
papers.what_to_take: The architecture SMAT and UniExo descend from (X. Zhou co-authors all three) and the dispute's lesson: claims without runnable code, seeds and model files now draw an editorial note.
papers.left_untested: Energy ratio (walking 5.5, stairs 6.6 J saved per J work per Collins) never reconciled with physiology in the paper; no independent replication with the learned network; no run-to-run variance.
papers.feasibility_notes: Cannot be rebuilt from public materials; treat numbers as disputed, not as reproduction targets.

papers.api_title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance remains an unsolved problem
papers.core_idea: Energy-ratio plausibility check: metabolic saving per unit exo positive work should not exceed ~4 (prior devices ≤2.3); Luo et al. imply 5.5 (walking: 61.6 W / 11.2 W) and 6.6 (stairs). Fixed-profile replication (N=10, 4.8 kg, four timing shifts) found no significant reduction.
papers.what_to_take: Adopt its checklist as the programme's reporting bar: executable code, reward parameters, PPO hyperparameters, seeds, learning curves, run-to-run variability, model files; add an energy-ratio sanity check to every metabolic claim.
papers.left_untested: Replicated the average torque profile, not the learned state-feedback network; no simulation replication of the learning pipeline, which is exactly what an open SMAT reconstruction could supply.
papers.feasibility_notes: Reading only; energy-ratio check is computable from simulated exo power and a muscle metabolic model.

papers.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
papers.authors_short: Luo, Jiang, Zhang, Zhu, Yu, Dominguez Silva, B. Zhou, Yuk, X. Zhou, Su

papers.api_title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
papers.core_idea: Rebuttal: the ratio 4 is an average muscle efficiency, not a ceiling; recomputes walking energy ratio as 2.4 (or 3.4 with 18% timing correction); says replication used a fixed averaged profile, heel-strike timing offsets up to 30%, and a 50% heavier device.
papers.what_to_take: Gait-event convention (heel strike vs torque-peak timing) changes estimated exo power and energy ratio (2.4–5.5 across the two papers); fix event definitions and power computation before comparing controllers.
papers.left_untested: No new hardware replication with the learned network, no released code at a checkable location, no seed-level simulation results; independent-results argument cites Barati (single-agent) and Zhou (3 participants).
papers.feasibility_notes: Reading only; note X. Zhou (SMAT senior author) co-signs this response, so SMAT is not independent of the dispute.

papers.title: Exo-Plore: Exploring Exoskeleton Control Space through Human-aligned Simulation
papers.code_status: full pipeline released: DART C++ sim, Ray RLlib PPO gait generator, parameter sampling, NN/GP surrogate, figure scripts; dataset via external SharePoint link, no checkpoints in repo; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; last push 2026-08-04 (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Exo-Plore: Exploring Exoskeleton Control Space through Human-aligned Simulation
papers.core_idea: Trains a musculoskeletal gait generator conditioned on hip-exo parameters with a human–exo interaction reward (metabolic plus resistance-minimisation), rolls out a delayed-output-feedback controller τ=κ·[sin q_r − sin q_l](t−Δt) over sampled (κ, Δt), fits a surrogate, and optimises per speed.
papers.what_to_take: A ready, coded simple-controller family (κ, Δt delayed output feedback) plus a human-adaptation reward (energy + interaction/resistance term) to build the programme's matched non-learned comparator arm in simulation.
papers.left_untested: No learned exo policy or co-adaptive (two-agent) comparison; no new hardware test of optimised parameters; DART human, not MyoAssist, so transfer of the optimal (κ, Δt) to SMAT's model is unknown.
papers.feasibility_notes: Ray/DART CPU training (10k–24k epochs; 'medium_pc' preset = 32 workers) fits the 64-core EPYC but watch 30 GB RAM; non-commercial licence.

papers.title: Reinforcement-Learning-Based Assistance Reduces Squat Effort with a Modular Hip–Knee Exoskeleton
papers.code_status: no code link in the arXiv record or abstract (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Reinforcement-Learning-Based Assistance Reduces Squat Effort with a Modular Hip--Knee Exoskeleton
papers.core_idea: NJIT RL-in-simulation controller mapping recent hip/knee angle and velocity histories to hip and knee torques, tested in 5 adults doing metronome squats: about 10% lower net metabolic rate vs zero-torque and no-exo, but reduced squat depth.
papers.what_to_take: Kinematic side effects accompany metabolic savings (smaller squat depth here, larger hip ROM in SMAT): report task kinematics beside every effort metric.
papers.left_untested: Per abstract: baselines only zero-torque and no-exo (no simple-controller arm), no sim-predicted savings compared, n=5 preliminary.
papers.feasibility_notes: Reading only; squat task is outside Phase 1 but its kinematic-side-effect lesson applies.

cluster_lessons: SMAT's Stage-4 exo reward Δt·Σ(0.3·û·ω̂ − 0.15·û² − 2·max(0,|û|−0.8)²) with ω̂ = clip(ω/2 rad/s, ±1) is maximised pointwise by û ≈ clip(ω̂, ±0.81): a saturating velocity-proportional (negative-damping) law. The Stage-3 reward 0.5·û²·sign(û·ω) is maximised by bang-bang û = sign(ω), which explains the saturated 'Stage 3 only' ablation. UniExo keeps the same 0.3/0.15 power term (2608.00715 Eqs. 5-6; 2609.19690 Eq. 9). The learned policy has to beat this closed form before 'co-adaptation learns timing' can be claimed.

The headline simulated number (10.1% hip-activation drop, 2603.07618) compares the Stage-2 human with the Stage-4 human, but Table S2 of 2608.00715 changes the human reward between them (muscle-effort weight 0.01→0.15, activation-rate 0.005→0.05, hip-activation 0→5.0, hip imitation weights→0). Reproduce it as published, then add a same-policy exo-OFF evaluation and a τ_max=0 Stage-4 control; otherwise part of the 'assistance' effect is a reward change.

The shared-critic two-actor structure is stock MyoAssist (Yuan et al. BioRob 2026 'adapted from' MyoAssist; network_index_handler in neumovelab/myoassist). SMAT's contribution is the stage schedule and exo rewards, specified in 2608.00715 Algorithm S1 and Tables S2-S4 (PPO lr 5e-5/3e-5, clip 0.15, 2048 steps/env, 32 envs, minibatch 16384, 20 epochs, entropy 0.001/0.003; ~320M/160M/1.1M/66M steps per stage). Still missing: exo MJCF (5.94 kg device), reference motion file, full human observation spec, code, checkpoints.

Compute: the authors report ~28 h per 100M steps on an 8-core Xeon (about 150 h for the whole curriculum). Their own follow-up (UniExo) already runs MuJoCo Warp + mjlab + rsl_rl at 3.7e4 steps/s with 2048-8192 envs on one Blackwell GPU, so 'SMAT on GPU' is infrastructure, not a publishable claim. Fitz-Yuan/mjlab_myosuite is an unmodified fork of MyoHub's early-prototype bridge (last upstream push 2026-03-06); MyoAssist 1.0 itself is CPU MuJoCo 3.4 + Stable-Baselines3.

Disclosure bar after the Luo dispute: Nature added an Editor's Note on data/code availability (27 Jul 2026); the Nature code link is still non-runnable pseudocode; the Luo reply says code was released but gives no location; a Collins co-author (Slade) asked for code in Sept 2024 (issue #5, unanswered). SMAT shares its senior author (X. Zhou) with Luo 2024 and the reply, promised code 'upon acceptance', and SMAT-Exo is still a placeholder. Publish code, configs, seeds, learning curves and checkpoints from day one.

Plausibility check to run in simulation: Collins et al. bound metabolic saving per unit exo positive work at about 4 (prior devices ≤2.3; Luo 2024 walking implies 5.5); SMAT-ext reports about 1.3 (47.9 W saving vs 36.1 W positive power). Report simulated muscle-metabolic saving per joule of exo positive work for every controller arm, and fix the gait-event convention first (the two dispute papers disagree mainly on timing).

Kinematic side effects: on hardware SMAT raised hip ROM from 44° to 62° (+41%) and peak flexion velocity to about 251°/s without changing cadence or stride length, which is what a negative-damping velocity law would do. A reconstruction should check whether the simulated human shows the same amplification; SMAT zeroes hip imitation in Stages 3-4, which permits it.

Public comparator code exists: Exo-Plore (DaebangStn/exo-plore; delayed-output-feedback τ=κ·u(t−Δt), CC BY-NC-SA, CPU Ray/DART) and a third-party MJX/MuscleMimic dual-PPO overlay with separate critics and matched-initial-state exo ON/OFF evaluation (Luk7-sb/myoassist-dual-ppo-control; one snapshot commit 2026-08-26, no data or checkpoints, simulation-only ±10 Nm). MyoAssist's ctrl_optim spline controllers are stance-phase (vGRF state machine, ankle-oriented), so a full-cycle bidirectional hip phase profile must be written.
occupied_claims: Four-stage human–exo curriculum with shared-critic PPO in MyoAssist yielding a positive-power hip policy that transfers without per-subject tuning — SMAT (Yuan, Androwis, Zhou; arXiv 2603.07618, IROS 2026).
Metabolic validation of a simulation-trained co-adaptive hip controller: −19.7% vs passive device, −9.1% vs no-exo, n=8, plus speed/terrain generalisation — Yuan et al., arXiv 2608.00715.

One co-adapted hip controller across walking, turning, running, backward walking and transitions, trained with MuJoCo Warp + mjlab and initialised from a hip-moment predictor — UniExo, arXiv 2609.19690.
Experiment-free learning-in-simulation hip controller with reported −24.3/−13.1/−15.4% metabolic rate for walking/running/stairs — Luo et al., Nature 2024 (under Editor's Note since 27 Jul 2026).
Energy-ratio implausibility of Luo et al. 2024 and a null fixed-profile hardware replication (N=10) — Collins et al., bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.04.01.715109.
Single-agent exo RL against a reflex-based musculoskeletal walker transferring to hardware with −15.2% net metabolic cost (n=8) — Barati et al., RA-L 2026.
Simulation-only optimisation of delayed-output-feedback hip gain and delay with a human-adaptation reward; optimal delay decreases with walking speed — Exo-Plore (Leem et al., ICLR 2026).
Single joint policy (synergy prior) for muscles and hip-exo torque over speeds and slopes, distilled to an IMU student with preserved torque profiles (r=0.82) — Park, Song, Kang, arXiv 2603.04166.
Heterogeneous MARL (MATD3, centralised training) for human–hip-exo coupling in OpenSim — Sun et al., MBEC 2026.
Offline validation of simulation-trained exo networks against open-source biological moments, with delay tuning — You & Zhou, arXiv 2603.07629.
open_gaps: Closed-form control arm: repeat SMAT's Stage-4 human training with the exo policy replaced by û = clip(ω/2 rad/s, ±0.8) plus the learned policy's measured slew-rate limit (and lagged variants), matched on RMS and peak torque; compare hip-activation change, positive-power fraction and hip ROM. Not run by SMAT, SMAT-ext or UniExo.

Reward-confound control: evaluate the Stage-4 human with exo torque zeroed, and train a τ_max=0 sham Stage 3-4 with identical rewards, to separate assistance from the Stage 2→4 reward change behind the 10.1%. Absent from all SMAT papers.

Full-cycle hip phase-profile arm: a bidirectional spline (flexion and extension peak times and magnitudes) or Exo-Plore's κ·u(t−Δt), optimised by CMA-ES inside the same MyoAssist human; no head-to-head with a co-adapted policy exists.

Seed-level reproducibility: at least 5 seeds per stage with learning curves and pre-registered tolerances on the 10.1% mean and per-muscle −13.5/−10.5/−9.7/−6.6%, answering Collins et al.'s run-to-run variability demand; no SMAT or UniExo seed variance is reported.

Is staging necessary? Compare the four-stage schedule with simultaneous training (as in Luo 2024) under an exo reward without the β·û² zero-torque attractor; SMAT's 'Stage 4 only' collapse (peak 0.14) conflates staging with that reward term.
Model sensitivity: rerun SMAT on myolegs26 vs MyoLeg-80 (UniExo's model) and under 75/50% strength scaling (Yuan BioRob 2026 protocol); whether the simulated gain survives model changes is untested.

Energy ratio in silico: simulated metabolic saving (muscle metabolics model) per joule of exo positive work for SMAT vs control arms, checked against Collins et al.'s bound of about 4; no SMAT-line paper reports it.

Sprint regime with cable limits: staged co-adaptation for 200 m sprinting with a tension-only cable actuator model (force-rate, slack, bandwidth limits). SMAT trained at 1.25 m/s with ideal ±25 Nm torque; UniExo's run skill uses ideal ±15 Nm torque behind a 6 Hz low-pass filter.
unverifiable: Luo et al. 2026 reply's statement that 'executable code, raw experimental data, and simulation files' were released: no URL in the preprint, no new IntelligentRobotLearning repository (last push 2025-06-03), and the Nature code statement still points to the pseudocode repo (checked 2026-09-23).
